A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same ANOVA-TPNN work and contain complete main texts and appendices. Text extraction and visual inspection support reliable comparison despite substantial layout changes and renumbering.

before.justification: v1 reports original synthetic, tabular and CelebA experiments, including prediction performance, component stability, selection accuracy and ablations.

after.justification: v4 retains these original experimental results in Section 4 and the appendices.

M1.justification: Section 3.4 changes the stated NBM-TPNN parameter sharing from theta_k across components to theta_|S|,k across components of equal cardinality, permitting different bases for different interaction orders. The principal ANOVA-TPNN construction and training procedure remain unchanged.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same three synthetic functions, nine standard tabular benchmarks, three high-dimensional datasets and CelebA scenarios. The California Housing interpretability example is relocated from Appendix D to Section 4.7, not newly evaluated.

E2.justification: Corresponding comparisons retain NAM, NBM, NODE-GAM, XGB, DNN, Spline-GAM, decision trees and the CelebA linear classifier. No comparator is added or removed within the matched experiments.

E3.justification: Section 4 and Appendix B retain the 70/10/20 splits, evaluation metrics, sample sizes, preprocessing, hyperparameter searches, NID interaction screening and concept-bottleneck training settings. No experimental protocol revision accompanies the NBM-TPNN formula change.

E4.justification: The basis-count, initialization, ReLU, sum-to-zero removal and post-processing analyses are retained, together with the SHAP, monotonicity and spline-outlier case studies. Moving the California Housing interpretation analysis into the main text adds no analysis.

E5.justification: Both versions retain the same repeated-experiment counts, five-fit visual illustrations and mean/standard-deviation reporting. No new uncertainty estimates, confidence intervals or significance tests appear.

E6.justification: Matched result tables, SHAP examples and plotted findings retain their values. For example, Table 3 keeps California Housing ANOVA-T2PNN RMSE at 0.512 (0.01); the importance scores moved from v1 Tables 14–15 to v4 Tables 7–8 also match.

T1.justification: Section 3.4 makes a limited change to the mathematical definition of NBM-TPNN by indexing its shared basis parameters by interaction order. Propositions 3.1–3.2, Theorem 3.3, Corollary 3.4 and all Appendix A proofs remain unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract narrows component estimation enabled by uniqueness from 'stably and accurately' to 'stably.' Accuracy claims remain in the introduction, and the main identifiability, approximation and competitive-prediction contributions are retained.

C2.justification: Section 3.1 similarly narrows the stated consequence of unidentifiability from unstable and inaccurate interpretation to unstable interpretation. Interpretations of the experimental results and the limitation concerning computationally demanding high-order interactions otherwise remain unchanged.

D1.justification: v4 adds a source-code release statement and repository pointer in the abstract, absent from v1. Appendix B retains the hardware, implementation packages, optimizer settings and hyperparameter ranges. The PDFs establish the new access information, not independently verified repository availability.

R1.justification: v4 adds Sobol (2001), 'Global sensitivity indices for nonlinear mathematical models and their Monte Carlo estimates,' to the functional ANOVA background in Section 2.2. The remaining research positioning is retained; most citation changes reflect conversion to author-year style.

P1.justification: Most prose and section organization are retained. v4 moves the interpretability discussion from Appendix D into Section 4.7, adds acknowledgements and a generic impact statement, and makes localized wording, affiliation and citation-style edits.

P2.justification: v4 converts the main text to a two-column conference layout and extensively repositions and resizes displays. It promotes the California Housing figure and tables into the main text and fixes overlapping appendix captions, including v1 Tables 8–10. All 22 figures and the corresponding table content are retained.

improvement.justification: v4 supplies code-access information, brings the worked interpretability example into Section 4.7, and fixes caption overlaps visible in v1's Appendix B. These provide concrete reproducibility and readability gains. The empirical evidence and principal theoretical guarantees are unchanged, so the overall improvement is limited.
